added.title: Integrated Watershed Management Business Class Lead for Water Resource Plan Formulation
added.description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

We believe water is more than a resource, it's a shared responsibility. As part of our Water Business Group, you’ll help shape how communities manage water for generations to come. From delivering safe drinking water and treating wastewater responsibly to developing sustainable water supplies and protecting lives and property through flood control, your work will directly support public health, environmental sustainability, and infrastructure resilience. We bring together experts across disciplines to solve complex challenges with bold thinking and technical excellence. Whether you're modernizing aging systems or pioneering innovative approaches, your contributions will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. This isn’t just a job, it's a chance to lead change, drive progress, and leave a lasting legacy.

The Business Class Lead (BCL) will work with the Business Class Director (BCD) and HDR peers on monitoring and improvement of technical competencies, staff development, and execution of work associated with water resource planning that meets federal planning standards and expectations. The overall goal of the role is to promote a quality culture, drive or support BC initiatives that drive growth and project delivery, and work with areas to hire, train and support career progression of staff within this technical service area.

The successful candidate will bring a vision for delivery, mentoring, and market growth; and have a proven ability to work broadly with teams to deliver positive outcomes for projects. The BCL will collaborate on business class efforts with market sector directors, business group regional directors, other business class leaders, local business group leaders, local market sector (marketing) leaders, cross sector leadership, and area staff.

The BCL responsibilities include the following:

Fostering a quality culture though project delivery excellence and staff coaching. Serve as a Quality Control lead, technical advisor, and technical lead (i.e., Project Manager or Task Manager) for specific projects. Work with project teams to field needs and align staff to meet delivery expectations and develop strategy to promote knowledge transfer and staff development within water resource plan formulation.
Leading or supporting Business Class sponsored standards and guidelines (i.e., best practices) technical tools, checklists, workflows, and techniques to enhance service quality and efficiency. Promoting forward thinking delivery and strategy approaches as well as technology use and adoption.
Participating in tactical planning including engagement others within HDR to align initiatives with market drivers and client needs. Maintain awareness related to industry trends and drivers. Implementing actions associated with annual planning including leading or supporting recruiting key positions in partnership with others.
Working with others within HDR including client facing and marketing staff to track, develop and share qualifications and project approaches. Engage on specific pursuits as a lead or team member. Drive industry facing strategies associated with technical service area (e.g., professional association engagement, webinars, workshops, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading plan formulation for Federal clients. Specific experience with the USACE’s Principles, Requirements and Guidelines (PR&G) ideal.
Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams to successful project outcomes.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience
A minimum of 10 years experience
Professional registration, license or certification may be required based on role
Strong communication and listening skills
Ability to handle multiple assignments
Good leadership and organizational skills
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

We provide a comprehensive benefits package that promotes employee ownership, employee health, performance, and success, which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, an employee assistance program, paid time away, parental leave, paid holidays, a retirement savings plan with employer match, employee referral bonus and tuition reimbursement. added.title: Environmental Health Safety Coordinator
added.description:
Summary

Arcadis, APM Group Inc., has an opening for an EHS Coordinator to join our team in Boise, ID.
In this field-based role you will assist in the development and continuous improvement of the Arcadis safety culture through direct on-site support, developing and conducting EHS training programs, and providing safety coaching and mentoring to the department.

Successful candidates will have a minimum of 1 year of experience in construction EHS-related work on a project site, ideally supporting semiconductor, life science, or related industrial high-tech projects. Other experience may be considered. Candidates must live within commutable distance to the project site.

Responsibilities

Act as a technical resource for construction management group on assigned project site(s).
Provide on-site safety support for construction management projects.
Review safety inspections and safety observations generated by field personnel and provide coaching to ensure continuous improvement.
Conduct EH&S training, including but not limited to orientations, topics relevant to ongoing work, and post-incident follow-up.
Conduct visits for on-site safety compliance and provide appropriate and timely feedback.
Participate in subcontractor kick-off meetings.
Participate in constructability review meetings with subcontractors.
Under supervision, review job hazard analysis (JHA).
Participate in Construction Incident Analysis Meetings.
Review and validate corrective action plan action items on site.
Daily duties include but are not limited to participating in the safety leadership team, safety coordination meetings, mass safety meetings, daily pre-task plans, daily field compliance audits.
Prepare and submit safety metrics, including leading indicators and lagging indicators, as needed per policy and team requirements.
Other duties as assigned.

Skills And Qualifications

1+ years’ construction safety experience preferred.
STS-C certification or equivalent a plus.
Semiconductor & Data Center construction experience preferred.
Bi-lingual in Spanish preferred; both written and verbal.
General understanding of current federal, state, and local safety regulations as well as industry consensus standards.
Excellent verbal, written, and communications skills.
Formal training in safety management (OSHA, formal education, or similar, or combination thereof).
Organized and efficient in time and task management.
Ability to work independently with some oversight.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.
Exposure to Procore, Bluebeam, and other software platforms in use.
Local candidates required. Ability to provide valid work authorization for US employment required.

Working Conditions

This field-based position will work primarily on a construction site with minimal time in an office. Environmental conditions may vary and could include, but not be limited to, hot and cold temperatures, severe/inclement weather, and other factors.
Noise levels will be high at times depending upon work location.
Must wear required PPE as required by Arcadis or host employer(s).
Due to cleanroom protocols, successful candidates may need to wear cleanroom coveralls and follow client hygiene protocols.
Frequent walking, occasional lifting of objects in excess of 20lbs, frequent standing required.

The Company

DPS Group, Inc. is proudly part of the Arcadis Group of Companies and is a global EPCM firm offering full-service solutions within the Life Sciences (pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical technology) and Advanced Technology (semiconductor, data center, and solar) industries. DPS is dedicated to delivering successful projects with a ‘client-first’ mentality and personal touch across a range of market sectors: Project and Program Management, Procurement, Design, Construction Management, Health and Safety Management, Commissioning, Qualification, and Start-up.

DPS Engineering Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer and employment selection decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and abilities. DPS does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of: race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by country, regional or local law.

added.title: Environmental Air Quality Modeler
added.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

At WSP, we are driven by inspiring future-ready pioneers to innovate. We are seeking an experienced Environmental Air Quality Modeler
to join our growing Environmental Team. This position offers the opportunity to work on complex air quality permitting, compliance, and modeling projects for a diverse portfolio of industrial clients throughout the United States.

This role is preferably based in our Columbus, Ohio office; however, qualified candidates may be located in any WSP office across the United States.
The successful candidate will collaborate with multidisciplinary teams nationwide to deliver innovative environmental solutions, support critical infrastructure and industrial development projects, and help clients navigate an evolving regulatory landscape.

The ideal candidate will bring strong technical expertise in air quality permitting and modeling, sound project management skills, and a commitment to delivering exceptional client service while helping shape sustainable outcomes for our communities and environment.

Your Impact

Lead and support air quality permitting, compliance, and regulatory projects for industrial clients.
Prepare and review New Source Review (NSR), Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD), and other air permit applications.
Conduct air dispersion modeling analyses using tools such as AERMOD and other applicable modeling platforms.
Perform emissions calculations, emissions inventories, and air regulatory analyses.
Prepare semi-annual, annual, and other regulatory compliance reports.
Interpret federal, state, and local air quality regulations and provide strategic guidance to clients.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary project teams to deliver high-quality environmental solutions.
Manage project scopes, schedules, budgets, and deliverables while ensuring technical excellence.
Build and maintain strong client relationships through responsive communication and trusted technical support.
Support business development initiatives, including proposal preparation, client engagement, and identification of new project opportunities.
Mentor junior staff and contribute to the continued growth and development of the Air Quality practice.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Meteorology, Environmental Science, or a closely related discipline.
5+ years of professional experience in air quality permitting, regulatory compliance, and environmental consulting.
Demonstrated experience with:
Air dispersion modeling.
New Source Review (NSR) permitting.
Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD) permitting.
Nonattainment permitting requirements.
Air emissions inventory development.
Title V permitting.
Regulatory compliance evaluations.
Air emission control technology assessments.

Experience performing PSD modeling using AERMOD.
Strong understanding of federal and state air quality regulations, policies, and emerging regulatory programs.
Excellent technical writing, communication, data analysis, and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and Word.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects, priorities, and client relationships simultaneously.
Proven ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within a team environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with both AERMOD and CALPUFF modeling platforms.
Existing professional relationships with state and federal regulatory agencies.
Experience working with the Texas, Ohio, Indiana, or Kentucky environmental regulatory agencies.
Air permitting and compliance experience within one or more of the following industries:
Utilities and Power Generation
Data Centers
Oil and Gas
Refining
Chemical Manufacturing
Industrial Manufacturing

Active participation in industry or environmental professional organizations.
Strong client management and business development experience.
Demonstrated ability to anticipate client needs and develop practical, solution-oriented recommendations.

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

www.wsp.com

WSP provides a flexible and agile workplace model while meeting client needs. Employees are also afforded a comprehensive suite of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, life, and retirement savings focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career.

At WSP, we want to give our employees the challenges they seek to grow their careers and knowledge base. Your daily contributions to your team will be essential in meeting client objectives, goals and challenges. Are you ready to get started?

WSP USA (and all of its U.S. companies) is an Equal Opportunity Employer Race/Age/Color/Religion/Sex/Sexual Orientation/Gender Identity/National Origin/Disability or Protected Veteran Status.

The selected candidate must be authorized to work in the United States.

Notice To Third Party Agencies

WSP does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters, employment agencies, or other staffing services. Unsolicited resumes include any resume or hiring document sent to WSP in the absence of a signed Service Agreement where WSP has expressly requested recruitment/staffing services specific to the position at hand. added.title: Environmental Analyst
added.description:
Meta is seeking an Environmental Analyst to support environmental monitoring and analytics critical to regulatory compliance of our international data center and network builds. This position will work on cross-functional program efforts for the large and growing global infrastructure portfolio during the pre-development, construction, and operations phases. This position will work closely with both the data center and network environmental teams, as well as our land management team, and will report directly to the Global Head of Environment within the Site Development organization. Some travel is necessary to visit our sites (up to 25%).

Environmental Analyst Responsibilities:

Own and evolve analytical frameworks for tracking Meta's global data center, network, and land management environment obligations, including portfolio dashboards, milestone and reporting tracking, and risk indicators
Design analytical approaches spanning the full environmental permitting lifecycle—integrating data from site selection, permitting, design, procurement, construction, and commissioning
Own the analytical data architecture for the environmental and land management team to inform reporting across multiple environmental disciplines (air, noise, cultural, biology, native habitat, contaminants, etc)
Drive automation of data collection, quality control/assurance, transformation, and reporting workflows to reduce manual effort and support compliance with environmental regulations and permits
Serve as an analytical integration point for stakeholders with the environmental and land management team
Design and document analytical methodologies, SOPs, and training materials that enable partners to self-serve for routine data needs

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related field
5+ years of experience in analytics, strategy, or environmental programs
Experience in designing analytical frameworks and executing complex multi-variable analyses independently
Experience building portfolio-level dashboards and reporting systems that drive executive decision-making
Experience communicating complex analytical findings to leadership and cross-functional partners through presentations, reports, or executive summaries
Proficiency in SQL, Python, or R for data manipulation and environmental data pipeline development, combined with experience in Tableau or Power BI for visualization

Preferred Qualifications:

Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize analytical workflows and drive measurable improvements in data quality, reporting efficiency, or decision-support speed
Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
Experience with federal and state environmental review processes such as NEPA, Clean Water Act Section 404, or state equivalents in the context of large-scale infrastructure developments
Experience designing and executing multi-variable analytical frameworks that integrate environmental, regulatory, and operational data to support capital project decisions
Familiarity with hyperscale data center development lifecycle phases, including site selection, environmental permitting, entitlement, and construction

added.title: Principal Consultant - Air Quality
added.description:
We are SLR Consulting (US), a 500+ coast-to-coast team of advisory, environmental/engineering, and regulatory professionals. We deliver environmental and sustainability services to our clients through the integration of over 30 advisory, technical environmental, and engineering disciplines to help clients address some of their most complex challenges around sustainability. We are Making Sustainability Happen.

As our new Principal Consultant
, you will play an important role on a team whose work is essential to achieving this goal.

Role

The Principal Consultant will be an integral part of our Air Quality Practice, supporting multimedia projects as a project manager, technical expert, and staff mentor. SLR believes strong collaboration across disciplines and staff levels drives business excellence and growth, and the Principal Consultant will be the essential link in cultivating these relationships. The highly experienced environmental science leader will be responsible for advancing regulatory compliance, air quality monitoring, sampling programs, and environmental program management across state and industrial settings. The candidate will provide expert scientific guidance, project leadership, and regulatory interpretation to support environmental protection, public health, and operational excellence.

As SLR continues to expand its presence and capabilities in Houston, the Principal Consultant will play a pivotal role in shaping the trajectory of our project portfolio. This position will contribute to growth opportunities across emerging and established markets, leveraging strong client partnerships and regulatory insight into the position of SLR as a preferred provider in environmental and air quality services. Through project development, cross ‑ disciplinary integration, and high ‑ caliber technical leadership, the Principal Consultant will help drive sustainable business expansion while ensuring that our project work consistently reflects innovation, compliance excellence, and industry ‑ leading best practices.

By mentoring team members, strengthening operational processes, and fostering a collaborative culture, the Principal Consultant will contribute directly to building a resilient, scalable operation. Their leadership will ensure the Air Quality Practice remains agile, competitive, and prepared to meet evolving industry demands—ultimately supporting SLR’s broader organizational mission to Make Sustainability Happen.

Responsibilities

Develop and mentor a growing team of environmental professionals, fostering a collaborative and high-performance culture.
Organize project teams, logistics and schedule to efficiently deliver projects.
Manage and contribute to the preparation of air quality permit applications (e.g., PSD, Title V, Minor Permit, AQADs).
Provide regulatory guidance and compliance support to clients across diverse industries.
Stay ahead of evolving environmental regulations and translate insights into client solutions
Ensure project delivery within scope, budget, and schedule expectations
Contribute to growing client relationships.

Qualifications/Education/Memberships

Proven track record in environmental consulting.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Environmental Science, Chemistry, or related field
15-20+ years of relevant experience in environmental consulting, government or industry (oil and gas, mining, utilities).
Strong knowledge of air quality regulations (Title V, PSD, NSPS, NESHAP, GHG, RMP, Ambient Monitoring)
Effective communicator, writer, with strong organizational and analytical skills
Proficient in Microsoft Office; valid driver’s license.

Working @ SLR

With us, there is no doubt you’ll grow your subject-matter expertise and industry knowledge. We care about investing in our employees for the long-run, and if you ask our team, they’ll tell you that’s just one of the many benefits of working here. We want to be a place where you can experience career growth and satisfaction for many years.

Here’s what else you’ll enjoy as part of our team:

Competitive total compensation package including medical, dental, orthodontia, vision, FSA/HSA, generous PTO accrual, 10 paid holidays, 401(k) retirement account with company matching program, company paid life insurance, short & long term disability insurance, and employee assistance program.
Part-time, permanent role with opportunities for professional growth and advancement
A flexible workplace environment for modern leaders
